title: Define post-merge certification equivalence and proof-reuse rules
objective: Define a pure fail-closed post-merge verifier that reuses prior certification only when the merged target is cryptographically tree-equivalent to the certified candidate and all promotion/provenance identities remain intact; otherwise require bounded revalidation instead of automatically rerunning the full suite.
non_goals: merge a pull request or mutate main
rerun the full historical test chain

required_invariants: post-merge verification is pure and never mutates Git PR lifecycle canonical business state or runtime authority
prior promotion decision must be PROMOTION_ALLOWED and bind the exact certified candidate head
merged target branch must be main and merged head/tree identifiers must be lowercase SHA-40
tree-equivalence reuse requires merged tree SHA to equal the certified candidate tree SHA exactly
candidate promotion provenance and certification verdict identities remain immutable inputs to the post-merge record
merge metadata must bind the source candidate id head and PR identity without ambiguity
tree mismatch candidate mismatch missing promotion evidence or unknown merge method returns REVALIDATION_REQUIRED
tree-equivalent merge may reuse prior certification semantics without rerunning full regression or T4
post-merge equivalence record is a new SHA-256 identity and never rewrites prior certification provenance
post-merge result never unlocks business Lot46 trading execution leverage or withdrawals
acceptance_criteria: candidate id or head mismatch produces REVALIDATION_REQUIRED
post-merge identity changes when merged head or merge metadata changes
reuse result explicitly records full_regression_rerun=false and t4_rerun=false
revalidation result never claims prior certification covers changed tree
no main PR business state Lot46 or runtime authority is mutated during qualification

done_when: tree-equivalent post-merge reuse is deterministic and cryptographically bound
any content drift fails closed to revalidation rather than automatic reuse
post-merge verification avoids redundant full-suite and T4 reruns only when equivalence is exact
business and runtime safety state remain unchanged
